tasks.short: Manipulate raw remote-sensing data to enhance interpretation.

steps.what: Inspect actual raw data files and reconcile sensor, acquisition time, coordinates, bands and calibration metadata
inputs: actual raw sensor files and metadata
existing acquisition and calibration records
outputs: checked raw input manifest with missing metadata

steps.what: Choose appropriate raw-data corrections, band combinations and display transforms for the actual interpretation need
inputs: checked raw input manifest with missing metadata
actual scientific interpretation requirement
outputs: technician-selected transformation parameters and limits

steps.what: Manipulate raw data into a derived working preview using native repeatable correction and display operations
inputs: checked raw input manifest with missing metadata
technician-selected transformation parameters and limits
outputs: derived working preview and actual processing log

steps.what: Check the actual enhanced data for geometric, radiometric and display artefacts against raw sources
inputs: derived working preview and actual processing log
actual raw sensor files and metadata
outputs: checked derived data and interpretation cautions

steps.what: Prepare the actual derived-data package with input IDs, processing parameters, quality findings and destination
inputs: checked derived data and interpretation cautions
derived working preview and actual processing log
outputs: complete enhanced-data package and provenance note

steps.what: Approve the finished enhanced-data version, provenance and internal dataset destination
inputs: complete enhanced-data package and provenance note
outputs: approved enhanced-data version

steps.what: Commit the approved enhanced data and provenance to the internal derived-data repository
inputs: approved enhanced-data version
outputs: versioned internal enhanced dataset

tasks.design: Configure native metadata views and repeatable transforms in {OTHER}, the existing remote-sensing image processor and GIS. {DATA_PLATFORM} holds raw and derived datasets; {DOCS} holds provenance notes. The technician reconciles actual metadata, chooses transforms and checks actual outputs. Reusable native settings reduce operator setup and repeated controls, not processing runtime. The derived working preview stays a draft until the complete package is approved and separately committed. Changes void approval. This is the ground-processing branch, with no flight control, onboard configuration change or generative image alteration.
tasks.previous_blocker: Raw data preparation repeats metadata checks and operator transformation setup.
tasks.enabler_now: Native repeatable transforms and metadata validation views.
tasks.still_hard: Sensor-specific artefacts and choosing scientifically appropriate enhancement.
tasks.human_edge: Recognize a persuasive enhancement that distorts the underlying observation.

ambition.what: Reduce repeated operator preparation of current raw datasets.

tasks.altitude: Scientific transformation choice and quality checking remain human.

reach.learn: Use the actual transform history and cautions alongside the raw source.

evidence.claim: Remote-sensing image processors support repeatable corrections, band combinations and metadata views.

assumptions: Shares are provisional human labour, not compute time. s1 manually captures or reconciles sensor/file ID, acquisition time, coordinate system, band, calibration version and source where metadata is missing.
s3 retains human setup, missing-data repair and operator exception handling; savings are repeated commands and parameter entry, never unattended processing duration.
s5 manually captures actual processing parameters and quality findings; selected settings are not proof that processing completed correctly.
This task owns individual raw-data enhancement. Mosaicking is task 16990; shared metadata preparation must be allocated once when both are performed on the same inputs.
unknowns: Sensor mix and native metadata completeness.
research_questions: How much operator work remains after metadata repair and actual output checks?

inputs: checked mosaic input manifest and unresolved gaps
technician-selected mosaic settings

inputs: actual working mosaic draft and merge log
actual scanned images

tasks.design: Configure native mosaic batch operations and georeference checks in {OTHER}, the existing GIS and raster image processor, before custom code. {DATA_PLATFORM} supplies actual inputs and stores the approved product; {DOCS} holds provenance. Human metadata reconciliation, seam decisions and actual output correction remain. Reused batch settings reduce operator controls only. Finish the actual mosaic and provenance before approval and a distinct repository commit. Changes void approval. No model fills gaps, invents pixels or resolves conflicting dates.
tasks.previous_blocker: Mosaics repeat image setup and merge controls across many tiles.
tasks.enabler_now: Native batch merging and reusable raster settings.
tasks.still_hard: Poor scans, weak control points and incompatible capture dates.
tasks.human_edge: Recognize when a visually smooth mosaic is geographically misleading.
tasks.altitude: Geographic quality and seam judgement remain human.

reach.learn: Read actual source dates and coverage limitations.

evidence.claim: Native GIS and raster processors can merge georeferenced images with reusable batch settings.

assumptions: Shares are provisional human work. s1 includes manual image ID, date, coordinate reference, extent and control-point capture when scans lack usable metadata.
Actual scanning or field acquisition remains separately counted source work; no new acquisition labour is shifted outside the graph to achieve these gains.
s3 saves repeated operator setup and commands, never processing runtime. s4 retains actual seam correction and gap resolution; missing ground information is not invented.
s5 manually captures actual input IDs, output version, merge settings and quality limitations. Raw-data enhancement in task 16998 is separate; overlapping metadata preparation must be allocated once.
unknowns: Actual scan quality and metadata repair effort.
research_questions: Do native batch operations reduce total human effort after seam and displacement checks?

tasks.design: Configure native coverage views and map layouts in {OTHER}, the GIS, with {DATA_PLATFORM} imagery references and {PROJECT} resource fields. Actual requirements, design discussion and project choices remain human. Native {DOCS} plan sections reuse checked maps and fields. Approve the finished contribution and exact {EMAIL} message before separate internal commit and send; changes void approval. This is a planning contribution, with no flight authorization, resource booking or externally binding project commitment. No model is needed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Mapping feasibility references and plan layouts are repeatedly assembled.
tasks.enabler_now: Native coverage views, reusable map layouts and project templates.
tasks.still_hard: Accuracy/resource trade-offs and incomplete terrain or sensor evidence.
tasks.human_edge: Choose a mapping approach appropriate to the actual objective.

ambition.what: Reduce preparation around mapping project planning.

tasks.altitude: Mapping design and collaboration remain human.

reach.learn: Keep unresolved coverage assumptions visible before commitments.

evidence.claim: Native GIS coverage views and reusable layouts can support mapping project plan preparation.

assumptions: Shares are provisional. s1 manually captures area, purpose, accuracy, date, deliverable and constraint; s2 manually verifies data IDs, date/coverage, sensor limits and actual resource availability when metadata is incomplete.
s4 manually captures chosen approach, rationale, unresolved assumptions and recipient; no completed brief or approved project plan is assumed free.

Project-lead adoption and commitments are existing downstream work with no saving claimed. Technical data processing and formal presentation production belong to their specific tasks; overlapping map preparation must be allocated once.
unknowns: Coverage metadata completeness and native project links.
research_questions: Does plan preparation improve after all actual requirement and feasibility checks?

tasks.design: Configure native GIS exports in {OTHER}, the GIS and raster viewer, and document/slide layouts in {DOCS}; {SPREADSHEET} computes exact charts and {DATA_PLATFORM} supplies actual approved outputs. The technician captures missing source facts and checks figure scales, dates and provenance. A bounded loop drafts captions and prose only from existing approved findings. The finished package and exact {EMAIL} message are reviewed before separate internal record and send steps. Changes void approval. No public publication or live presentation delivery is included.
tasks.previous_blocker: Figures, source labels and explanatory sections are repeatedly assembled.
tasks.enabler_now: Native figure exports and layouts plus checked prose drafting.
tasks.still_hard: Honest geographic explanation and communicating uncertainty.
tasks.human_edge: Choose what an audience needs to see and understand.
tasks.altitude: Scientific meaning and final communication remain human.

reach.learn: Trace displayed claims to actual approved data and limitations.

evidence.claim: Native GIS exports and document templates can assemble scientific figures; a bounded language-model loop can draft source-linked prose requiring review.

assumptions: Shares are provisional. s1 includes manual capture of source ID/version, date, coordinate system, units, photo rights and audience requirements where metadata is incomplete.
s2 includes actual layout, scale, legend and figure checks, not processing runtime. s3 includes source-fidelity correction and manual capture of approved findings and limits.

Scientific analysis is existing separately counted work, not newly transferred to others. This task owns document assembly; image enhancement, mosaics and mapping plan contributions are separately owned and shared preparation must be allocated once.
Internal handover is modeled. Public or client delivery and live presentation require their own final-version gate and separately counted actions.
unknowns: Native layout reuse and source metadata quality.
research_questions: How much assembly effort survives after checking every geographic and numerical claim?
